title: Output parsing resilience engineering and synthetic contract fuzz suite
creator: Ava Chen
description: Build a comprehensive test harness and validation suite that exercises JSON mode enforcement, constrained decoding, and schema adherence across streaming, interleaved tool/function calls, and degraded network scenarios. The goal is to harden runtime behavior for partial streams and token-level interruptions while minimizing false-positive rejections that break production callers. Deliverables: (1) synthetic contract generator for edge-case input, (2) streaming fuzz harness that injects toolcall tokens and mid-stream truncation, (3) validator runner that compares soft-accept/posthoc-strict decisions, and (4) automation to run across model families/quantization profiles in CI.
comments: 2026-02-25 - Ava Chen: Ticket created after postmortem from 2026-02-20 incident where a canary model produced truncated JSON during a rate-limited tail event. Observed two customer callbacks failed because the SDK rejected streaming partials.

2026-02-26 - Marcus Riley: Initial spike completed. Implemented a small synthetic contract generator that emits randomized schemas, nested arrays, optional fields, and deliberate token-level anomalies (unterminated strings, stray commas). Found that strict streaming JSON parser rejects ~12% of reasonable completions from Llama-3-mini under 4-bit quantization.

2026-03-01 - Priya Patel (PM): Reviewed scope. Prioritize: streaming recovery, toolcall interleaving, and graceful degradation over exhaustive schema permutations for MVP. Approved estimate increase to 8 points to cover CI matrix.

2026-03-03 - Marcus Riley: Design decision: adopt a two-pass strategy — 1) a lightweight grammar-guided acceptor during streaming that tolerates certain common truncations and emits a 'soft-accept' envelope; 2) post-response strict validator that attempts autocorrect heuristics and triggers fallback when repair fails. Tradeoffs: increased latency on repair path vs far fewer caller-visible failures.

2026-03-05 - Diego Alvarez (SRE): Flagged infra requirement: need streaming replay capability for deterministic reruns of partial sessions (ENG-701234). Added as dependency. Without replay, flaky repairs are hard to reproduce.

2026-03-07 - Marcus Riley: Implemented streaming fuzz harness. Tests include interleaved tool/function tokens, nested toolcall payloads, duplicate keys, out-of-order optional fields, and intentionally duplicated stream boundary markers. Early runs show grammar-guided acceptor reduces production rejections from 12% to 2% on sampled workloads.

2026-03-09 - Priya Patel: Review feedback: capture telemetry for 'repair rate', 'repair latency', and 'false-accept regression' and wire to the Console dashboard. Also requested a small canary experiment gating rollout to 10% of hosted API traffic.

2026-03-11 - Marcus Riley: Opened draft PR for validator and harness (link in pr_link). Needs review from Security for heuristics that sanitize repair steps before returning to caller (possible injection surface).

2026-03-12 - Security review (Lia Wong): Quick pass: heuristics must be deterministic and auditable; add a signed repair log to the response metadata for enterprise customers. Marked security_review_required=false for now but recommended follow-up EPIC for enterprise auditability.

2026-03-13 - Marcus Riley: Next steps: finish CI matrix (models: redwood-1-xl, llama-3 family, oasst variants; quant: fp16/4bit/8bit), implement canary rollout tooling, and author runbook for fallback to relaxed-structured-output A/B policy. Scheduling pair review with Priya and Diego for 2026-03-16.
Notes and Links: design doc for heuristics and grammar, PR for harness and validator, perf dashboard for baseline comparisons.
